title: Volume 1 Chapter 9: Reserve Forces
content: Chapter 9: Reserve Forces
“The experiment was a success, wasn’t it? …Congratulations, Ren-kun.”

Louise’s silver hair fluttered in the wind on the rooftop as she smiled faintly, a trace of sadness in her eyes. She was celebrating the success of the experiment against the backdrop of the setting sun, but it seemed she wasn’t truly happy from the bottom of her heart. I already had a rough idea why.
“I feel sorry for you, Louise. But in my case, it seems facing magic power with a negative mindset was the right choice.”
From Louise’s perspective, who had advised me to think positively, prioritizing Lieutenant Hayase’s opinion must have felt like a betrayal. Yet, Louise did not blame me.
“Don’t worry about it. I’m just glad you found the best method for yourself. Still… I want you to become more positive, Ren-kun.”
“Why is that?”

Although I accepted myself as I am and succeeded, trying the old method again now would mean a step backward for the project. It was a proposal I didn’t want to accept, but Louise seemed to have her reasons.
“It’s fine to accept yourself. But that doesn’t mean negative emotions are okay. I’m worried that someday you might spiral down the wrong path.”
“No problem. The project is progressing smoothly, and the development team is working tirelessly to make up for lost time.”
“Still… I’m worried.”
Louise looked down, clutching the hem of her skirt, then raised her face to look at me.
“Ren-kun, can I ask you something?”
“If it’s something I can answer.”
“What are these negative emotions of yours? What made you use magic power?”

Her eyes were serious, fixed on me. Was I allowed to answer? Louise, as an ally, had permission to know part of the experiment’s details, but the criteria regarding me personally were vague. However, when it came to magic power, the Valkyries knew more than we did. For the future, I decided to be honest with her.
“…Jealousy.”
“Jealousy?”
Louise tilted her head in confusion. I looked away and gazed at the sunset as I spoke.
“When I was infantry, I often looked up at the Valkyries flying in the battlefield sky. My squadmates teased me about it, but my eyes naturally followed them.”
Louise listened intently, her expression gradually becoming blank.
“Isn’t that admiration?”
Admiration might sound better, but I understood myself best. The feeling I had was unmistakably jealousy.
“No, it’s not.”
“…It’s not?”
I shifted my gaze to her face and saw a slight look of disappointment. She quickly changed her expression and smiled, clasping her hands behind her back.
“But someday, I want you to handle magic power with positive emotions. Lieutenant Hayase seems to be scheming something too, and I’m worried you might be used.”
Louise’s caution toward Lieutenant Hayase made me bring up a question I’d had for some time.
“I have some questions about Lieutenant Hayase.”
“Hm? What is it?”
Watching Louise tilt her body slightly, I pictured Lieutenant Hayase’s personality.
“Is Lieutenant Hayase really dangerous? I talked with her before, but it felt a bit different from what you said.”
The advice Lieutenant Hayase gave me didn’t feel like she was trying to stop the project, as Louise suggested. Rather, I sensed something else.
“Maybe I’m too harsh on her. Sorry. There were some things before, so maybe I’m biased.”
Louise admitted her opinion was biased but warned me.
“But still… it’s true you should be careful with Hayase. I don’t know what she’s thinking by getting close to you, but she still opposes the project.”
“That’s true.”

Lieutenant Hayase was also against the Prometheus Project. She gave me advice because she had no complaints about me. Louise, sitting to my left and looking at the sunset, urged me to be wary of Hayase.
“This advice worked out this time, but in the long run, I think it’s a negative. They’re rushing short-term success too much.”
I couldn’t say in front of Louise that the short-term method was the most welcome for continuing the project. I couldn’t tell her the project had almost been scrapped.
“Be careful, Ren-kun. Hayase might have gotten close to you to spy and gather information.”
Lieutenant Hayase approaching me to play spy? I shook my head, thinking it impossible.
“I can’t imagine the ace, Lieutenant Hayase, doing such a thing.”
“You’re naive! Naive, Ren-kun!”
“Huh?”
Suddenly, Louise leaned in close and strongly protested my misunderstanding.
“That kind of thing is everyday business here! It’s normal.”
“Normal!?”
I knew there were ways to get close to someone kindly and achieve your goals, but a school where that was everyday seemed strange.
“I can’t imagine Valkyries spying.”
I asked honestly, and Louise crossed her arms, ready to teach me, the naive one.

“We’ve been rivals competing since middle school before transferring here. If it helps gain even a little advantage, we don’t hesitate to deceive each other. Hayase grew up in that environment—do you think she can’t do the same?”
Was this skill honed by the harsh competition to knock down rivals? My image of the academy where Valkyries trained crumbled.
“I thought the academy was a place of fair and square competition.”

“You’re too naive, Ren-kun. At that rate, you’ll easily be fooled by girls. Be especially careful of those who approach you with flirty attitudes. You never know what they’re thinking behind your back.”
“Y-Yes.”

Louise’s words reminded me of what MC and Hairset had said. They liked to hang out with women but often ended up hurt, proudly telling their stories. I never understood why they boasted about failures. They said, “Women are good liars, so be careful.” Now I remembered their warnings mixed with nostalgia and loneliness.
“…I feel ashamed that I know so little.”
When I confessed honestly, Louise chuckled.
“I don’t dislike that about you, Ren-kun.”
“Thank you for your kindness.”
I thanked her, and she smiled with a slightly exasperated look.
“That’s not what I meant though… wait!?”
The mood was becoming friendly, but the siren blaring through the school building shattered it.
“What’s that sound?”
Looking around at the unfamiliar siren, Louise grabbed my left arm.
“It’s a scramble! We in Class 5 have to get to the classroom immediately!”
Pulled by Louise, I headed from the rooftop toward the Class 5 classroom, staring at my left hand she held.
“I heard Class 5 is reserve forces?”
As we hurried down the stairs, I asked, and Louise answered breathlessly.
“We’re out of the main force, but this time Class 3 is on scramble standby, so they requested reserve forces to cover the shortage.”
I’d heard before that Class 3 was rebuilding their strength and had the fewest Valkyries. I never thought Class 5 would be called on to fill the gap.
“Can’t reinforcements come from other classes?”

“Class 2 just finished standby and is on leave, and the others are busy with training and regular missions, so they usually don’t sortie. If the Gate’s scale was large, that’d be different, but this seems like a normal sortie.”
From the siren and announcements, Louise judged this was a routine deployment. The four classes rotated regularly, and changes were rare.
When we reached the floor with Class 5, Louise ran ahead of me.
“Besides, this is a chance for us to show our skills.”
When we arrived at the Class 5 classroom, over half the female students had already gathered. More kept coming, all looking tense. When about seventy percent had assembled, the instructor entered.
Everyone stood and saluted. The instructor glanced around, snorting with slight displeasure.
“Seventy percent. Not bad.”
Latecomers rushed in, pale at the sight of the instructor.
“S-Sorry!”
The instructor’s attitude was cold.
“Those late will be removed from sortie candidates. As you know, the Boots Cat Battalion’s Class 3 is on scramble. They requested reserve forces due to lack of numbers…”
The instructor scanned the nervous students and called names from a tablet. The top performers and those she favored were named.
“…Finally, Louise Durand. That’s all. Those called, change and head to the transport aircraft. Confirm your Battle Dress armaments.”
The instructor finished and hurried out. The remaining girls reacted variously. Those not called or late regretted it.
“I thought I’d be called next time!”
“I ran back from the dorm but was told I’m too late. That’s harsh!”
While some lamented missing their chance, most called cheered.
“Alright! This time I’ll shine and escape Class 5!”
The rough-mouthed girl imagined being scouted by other classes after this sortie.
“Uuuu, it’s my first battle, so I’m nervous…”
A quiet girl was overwhelmed by fear of her first real fight.
“Calm down. And don’t shoot your allies by overdoing it. You’ll lose points and your chance to transfer.”
A composed girl warned, and the rough one snorted.
“Words from a senior close to graduation carry weight. If you don’t transfer this time, there won’t be a next, right?”

Girls who spent three years in Class 5 were forced to graduate after being declared unfit for combat. For the calm girl, this was likely one of the few chances left to prove herself. She understood this, glaring sharply at the provocation but saying nothing.
Louise placed her hand on her chest and sighed softly.
“Good. I was called. This leads to the next chance.”
“If it’s Louise, she’ll definitely deliver results. I’m rooting for you.”
Louise smiled shyly at that.
“Thank you.”
At that moment, I received a message on my device.
“Excuse me… Is this Dr. Smith?”
It wasn’t the usual Dr. Allison contacting me, which caught my attention. Louise seemed curious too.
“What’s wrong?”
“…I’ve been ordered to deploy.”
The Thunderbolt, still in the middle of experiments, had been ordered to sortie.
In the hangar, Dr. Smith awaited me.
“I’ve been waiting, Envy. Wow, things have gotten serious.”
I saluted as Dr. Smith approached. He scratched his head and smiled wryly, an odd reaction for such a situation. I doubted he fully grasped the emergency, but he should understand it better than I.
“Deploying an experimental machine was unexpected.”
The magic power output experiment had just succeeded, and the project had moved to the next phase. I thought deploying it now was too soon, but maybe there was an extraordinary reason.
Dr. Smith smiled and answered my question.
“Actually, I asked the principal to deploy it if there was a chance. I didn’t expect the opportunity to come so soon.”
“…So you were the cause, Dr. Smith.”
Without shame, he explained how it came to this.
“You didn’t think they’d really approve, right? But since the timing was perfect, I decided to deploy it. So Allison and the team are rushing to arm the Thunderbolt.”
Looking where Dr. Smith pointed, the development team was fitting weapons onto the Thunderbolt. Dr. Allison shouted orders to her subordinates.
“Leave the large rifle for later! First, mount the Gatling gun on the left arm. Don’t forget the large drum magazine on the left shoulder!”
A large-caliber Gatling gun was brought in by forklift. The drum magazine was huge, and they were attaching it to the left shoulder with a special arm.
“Is that the weapon for the humanoid machine?”
Dr. Smith adjusted his glasses beside me and explained the armaments.
“The Gatling gun isn’t handheld but mounted on the left arm. Its caliber is even larger than what the Valkyries use.”
“...Large caliber means nothing against Gijuu. With my current magic power output, I’m maxed out on buoyancy and defense, so I can’t spare any for weapons.”

The Thunderbolt could fly alone, but magic power gave it buoyancy, reducing fuel and propellant consumption. I could cut buoyancy magic in a worst-case scenario, but I couldn’t cut the force field protecting the armor.
Only one Thunderbolt was prepared as an experimental machine. Losing it would mean the Prometheus Project’s failure.
Dr. Smith laughed at my words.
“That’s fine. What we want from you is just to get a feel for the battlefield.”
“...A feel for the battlefield?”
At first, I was surprised and suspicious—why now make me experience the battlefield? But Dr. Smith explained his intention.
“We want to see if you can maintain magic power output under battlefield conditions. You know, if tension or excitement makes it unstable, that’s a problem.”
“I see. …Then, was all this armament necessary?”
I noticed small missile containers on both legs and a large missile container on the right shoulder. Dr. Allison was sweating as she continued working and directing her team.
“Don’t forget the daggers behind the knees!”
If I had to describe the Thunderbolt’s current state, it was an armory. The heavily armored machine was loaded with weapons to the brim, making me worry if it could move properly.
“Isn’t that too much armament just to participate?”
I asked simply, and Dr. Smith shrugged before answering.
“When I reported the project had moved to the next phase, the upper management was thrilled and prepared the weapons.”
“They have high expectations.”
It wasn’t a bad thing if the Prometheus Project was expected to succeed. But Dr. Smith was laughing at me.
“Did I say something strange?”
He shook his head.
“No, you’re expected to do well too. The daggers behind the knees were specially prepared for you.”
“For me?”
Honestly, I wondered if I was worth that much effort. Dr. Smith began talking about my past combat data.
“You fought with dual daggers, right? You seemed to have quite the results.”
“That was when I was infantry. Whether it works the same in a humanoid machine is unknown.”
“Still, we’re setting up the environment so you can succeed.”
As we talked, Dr. Allison glared sharply at us.
“You two! Don’t look so idle when it’s busy! Especially the pilot, change quickly and wait in the cockpit!”
I straightened up, saluted, and said,
“S-Sorry!”
Dr. Allison’s sharp glare cut through our conversation.
Startled, I straightened my back, snapped to attention, and saluted.
“S-Sorry!”

I hurried to change into my pilot suit, the weight of the upcoming mission settling on my shoulders. The hangar buzzed with activity as the development team continued outfitting Thunderbolt with its heavy armament. The large rifle was still waiting to be mounted, but the gatling gun was already secured to the left arm, and the massive missile container was being attached to the right shoulder.
As I approached the cockpit, Dr. Smith caught up to me.
“Ready, Envy? This is a big step for the Prometheus Project.”

I nodded, gripping the control stick as I climbed into the pilot seat. The cockpit was cramped but filled with an array of instruments and displays, all designed to monitor and regulate the magic power output and weapon systems.
Dr. Allison’s voice came over the intercom, firm and commanding.

“Envy, remember, your primary objective is to test the magic power output under battlefield conditions. Don’t overextend yourself. The weapons are there if you need them, but survival and data collection come first.”
I acknowledged her with a nod, feeling the familiar mix of anxiety and determination.

The engines roared to life as I initiated the ignition sequence. Thunderbolt’s systems hummed, and the force field flickered into existence around the armored frame. Magic power surged through the conduits, granting the machine buoyancy and defensive strength.
“Let’s see if I can live up to their expectations,” I muttered, gripping the controls tighter.
As Thunderbolt lifted off, the hangar doors opened to reveal the dusky sky. The transport aircraft awaited nearby, ready to ferry the Valkyries and support units to the gate site.
The mission was no longer just an experiment—it was real combat.
I took a deep breath, steeling myself for what lay ahead.
